sources.title: À La Carte Homeschool | River Tech · Find their voice. Share the stage.
sources.content:
Find their voice. Share the stage.
Music, theater, voice, and movement give students a place to express themselves and create something together. Monday brings them into the rehearsal room, where individual effort becomes a shared performance.
[Image: River Tech students performing on stage]
A glimpse of learning at River Tech.
A place for every voice
Performing arts are central to life at River Tech. Students explore singing, acting, choir, and stagecraft with a team of six teachers and production leaders. Confident performers have room to stretch; students finding their voice receive encouragement and practice. Both learn to listen, communicate, and contribute.
Real productions. Shared accomplishment.
Students prepare full musical theater productions and community concerts throughout the year. They learn what it takes to carry a performance from rehearsal to opening night: knowing their part, responding to direction, and supporting the ensemble. Costumes and props help bring the story to life, with each member of the team contributing to the finished production.
10:25–12:00Aladdin & Christmas Concert
Production rehearsals, costumes, and props.
Non-performers: younger students have music and art; older students work on projects.
LunchLunch rotation
12:45–2:20Peter & Alice: The Way Home
Talent Show & Summer Concert preparation.
Non-performers begin at 1:00: younger students have P.E. and reading, then SuperBook and games. Older students have music or study hall, then art. See the full schedule for times.
2:20–2:30Clean up & get ready for pickup
[Image: Dan Hegelund]Dan Hegelund, Arts Director
Dan is a professional vocal coach, musician, and choir director. His experience includes studio recordings, radio and television broadcasts, and performances at the Presidential Palace of Ukraine, for the Latvian Government, and with Clash of the Choirs, the Coca-Cola Holiday Caravan, and the Northwest Folklife Festival. He brings that experience into rehearsals as students develop their voices, prepare their roles, and learn to perform together.
[Image: Caitlin Relvas]Caitlin Relvas, Dance Director
Caitlin has spent much of her life studying and teaching dance. She holds a B.A. in English and Classical Civilizations with a minor in Dance. Her teaching connects movement with expression, helping students develop stage presence and confidence through practice.
Angie FarbCostumes
Angie leads costumes for River Tech’s productions, working alongside Caitlin and the performing arts team to bring the characters and their world to the stage.
Kara McArthurProps
Kara brings experience with stage sets and eight years of teaching in Sunday school and children’s church. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Biblical Studies from Indiana Bible College and has organized educational events and field trips for homeschool families for a decade. At River Tech, she plans props and scenic elements, from marketplace details to the Cave of Wonders.
Charlotte TebowPerforming Arts
Charlotte helps shape River Tech’s productions from preparation through rehearsal. Her work on Aladdin includes preparing the script, organizing audition materials, selecting and editing song versions, and coordinating ideas for dances with Evelyn and Caitlin.
Evelyn HegelundPerforming Arts
Evelyn works with the performing arts team on River Tech’s productions. She collaborates with Charlotte and Caitlin on dance plans and helps prepare performance materials for the cast.

sources.title: À La Carte Homeschool | River Tech · Understand the world. Learn to live wisely.
sources.content:
Understand the world. Learn to live wisely.
Science helps students understand the natural world. Social studies explores people, places, and civilizations. Tuesday brings these subjects together with practical lessons in money, relationships, and leadership.
[Image: River Tech students watching a science demonstration]
A glimpse of learning at River Tech.
Understand the world around them
Students investigate, experiment, and ask questions in science. Big Picture Geography connects places with creation, history, and human civilization. With an approximately 1:12 student-to-teacher ratio and a competency-based approach, teachers can give students personal attention as they build understanding and master concepts.
Prepare for everyday life
Financial literacy and social development are taught with each age group in mind. Younger students learn about money and how to make and keep friends. Older students study personal finance, family life, and leadership. These classes connect schoolwork with decisions and responsibilities students will encounter beyond the classroom.

sources.content:
Think clearly. Create with confidence.
Clear thinking, thoughtful writing, and creative work belong together. Thursday gives students time to develop their ideas, express them well, and consider the convictions that guide their lives.
[Image: River Tech students creating pottery]
A glimpse of learning at River Tech.
Skills that shape a person
In writing and debate, students practice explaining an idea, examining the reasons behind it, and listening carefully to others. Fine art and crafts give them another way to explore and express what they see. In a small school where teachers know students and their families, these lessons become opportunities for personal guidance as well as skill development.
Faith, character, and direction
Our Christian faith connects learning with character and purpose. Students are encouraged to consider how their choices affect others and how their abilities can be used well. We want them to grow in wisdom, confidence, and a sense of responsibility to their community.

sources.content:
Turn curiosity into something that works.
On Fridays, students turn ideas into working projects through coding, robotics, filmmaking, and digital arts. Beginners and experienced tinkerers alike can develop the skills to create with technology.
[Image: River Tech students with a robotics project]
A glimpse of learning at River Tech.
Create with technology
Students write code, build and program robots, and explore digital tools, including AI. Projects connect technical skills with a purpose: what are we trying to make, who will use it, and how can we improve it? The work gives students practice in testing ideas, solving problems, and learning from mistakes.
Build skill. Develop judgment.
Technical confidence matters most when it is paired with good judgment. Students learn to understand the tools they use, question their limitations, and choose them thoughtfully. The aim is to help students create useful things and make informed decisions about technology.

sources.title: Enrollment & Wait Pool | River Tech · A few thingsworth knowing.
sources.content:
A few thingsworth knowing.
We want you to understand both the opportunity and the commitment.
Full-time or part-time?
We offer both. Full-time school serves grades 1–12, with four or five days a week of core academics, performing arts, and technology. Our part-time À La Carte program lets homeschool students ages 9–15 join us for one to four days a week.
You can indicate either program, or both, on the wait-pool form.
Explore full-time school → / Explore À La Carte →
What does it cost?
Joining the wait pool is free. Tuition depends on your program, attendance days, and payment plan. Review the current rates and household enrollment fee before joining so you know what to expect if a place becomes available.
Compare tuition and payment plans →
What if we need financial assistance?
The wait-pool form asks whether enrollment would depend on a River Tech scholarship. Tell us there so we understand your situation. Joining does not guarantee financial assistance or a place.
Read about financial assistance →
Can a child start during the school year?
Yes, when an appropriate seat is available. Tell us your preferred timing on the wait-pool form, including whether you can be flexible.
What should we know about the school’s culture?
River Tech is a Christian school. Prayer, worship, and biblical teaching are part of school life, and every program reflects a Christian worldview. Before joining the wait pool, read our culture page and consider whether it describes the community you want for your family.
Get to know our culture →

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Let’s go bowling!
sources.content:
Let’s go bowling!
Our next field trip is coming up! On Wednesday, November 4, we’re heading to River City Lanes Bowling. Both full-time and part-time students are welcome to join us!
$12 per bowler · Sign up & pay by Sunday, November 1, at midnight.
Sign up & pay ↗
Where & when
Location: River City Lanes Bowling / Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026 / Bowling time: 10:00–11:30 AM / Cost: $12 per person, including bowling, shoe rental, and taxes.
Full-time students
Full-time students joining the field trip should be dropped off at school between 8:10–8:30 AM and picked up at 2:30 PM, as usual. Transportation will be provided by our school bus, although a few Junior High and High School students may ride with Jordan, Caitlin, Luke, or Mary.
Part-time students
Meet us at River City Lanes at 9:45 AM and pick up by 11:30 AM. You are welcome to join us for park play after; see the school schedule below.
Part-time students must have a supervising adult. For this specific field trip, part-time students ages 13 and older may be dropped off with a River Tech teacher, without their own supervising adult. For students ages 12 and younger, text Mary to request permission to drop off your child without a supervising adult, if needed and if your child is independent enough.
Activities & cost
Bowling: $12 per participant, including shoe rental and taxes. Payment is collected through the sign-up form. River City Lanes will have a cosmic light show and song requests!
Arcade games: Optional! Students may bring extra cash to play arcade games. Not included in the bowling fee.
Food & snacks: The full River City Lanes menu will be available for purchase. Students may also bring their own cold lunch, snacks, or small treats to share with classmates and friends.
Costumes: Students are welcome to dress up! Please avoid costumes that may frighten younger children. No face-covering masks, weapons, blood, or gore.
Part-time student chaperones: If you would like to bowl, please sign up through the form and pay the $12 fee. If you are only coming to supervise, there is no need to sign up or pay. Just show up with your registered student.
School schedule for November 4
There will be no school that day for students who are not participating in the field trip.
For participating full-time students, we will begin with our usual morning assembly and have Math and English classes before and after the field trip. Weather permitting, we also plan to visit the Real Life outdoor and indoor playgrounds from 11:45 AM–12:45 PM before returning to school. Part-time students are welcome to join us at the playgrounds as well if they would like, with their supervising adult!
Please note that the schedule and playground destination are subject to change.
If you need to drop off your full-time student late or pick them up early, please text their Math or English teacher directly to coordinate. If you are unsure whom to contact, text Mary.
Sign-up & payment
Deadline: Sunday, November 1, at midnight (Pacific time).
Complete the form and payment to reserve your student's spot. If you miss the deadline, text Mary to check whether space is still available. Spots cannot be guaranteed after Sunday. Late places require Mary's approval and payment to Mary in cash.
Text Mary: 425-444-2271
Looking forward to a fun day with your students! 🎳
Sign up & pay ↗
Nov 4

These events have ended. The announcements below are archived for reference. Registration, payment, and volunteer sign-ups are closed.
All River Tech families
Trip overview
Dear parents,
Next week, River Tech students have two exciting field trips:
Wednesday, September 16 — Hidden Acres Farm and Student Farmers Market
Thursday, September 17 — NIC Robotics Department Tour for full-time high school students
One of our favorite annual field trips is back! Students will visit Hidden Acres Farm at Green Bluff, pick fresh produce, and then sell it to River Tech families at our Student Farmers Market at 2:15 PM that afternoon.
Student Farmers Market · 2:15 PM
The Student Farmers Market will take place on the lawn to the right of the school entrance. Please do not park on the right side of the school so we can keep that area open for the market.
Please come support our students at 2:15 PM! Bring cash—especially small bills—and bags for your purchases. All proceeds will help cover field-trip expenses. The students will be excited and proud to sell the produce they picked!
We need several parents of full-time students to volunteer as chaperones at Hidden Acres Farm from 10:45 AM to 1:00 PM. If you are available, please text Mary at 425-444-2271.
Full-time families
Hidden Acres Farm
Wednesday, September 16 | 8:30 AM–2:30 PM / Cost: $10 per full-time student
Full-time students
The $10 cost includes:
School-bus transportation
Teacher supervision
Produce picked by the student and sold at the market
Students will begin the day at school at 8:30 AM with Math and English. The bus will leave at approximately 10:00 AM and return in time for the Student Farmers Market.
Student Farmers Market · 2:15 PM
The Student Farmers Market will take place on the lawn to the right of the school entrance. Please do not park on the right side of the school so we can keep that area open for the market.
Please come support our students at 2:15 PM! Bring cash—especially small bills—and bags for your purchases. All proceeds will help cover field-trip expenses. The students will be excited and proud to sell the produce they picked!
Participation in this field trip is optional, but there will not be a separate on-campus program for students who choose not to attend. Students may take their Math and English workbooks home on Tuesday to complete their assignments.
Please carefully read the information below. Full-time students must sign up and pay through the form attached below by Sunday, September 13, unless other arrangements have been made with Mary.
Please complete the Hidden Acres registration and payment form below by Sunday, September 13.
Registration closed.

Part-time homeschool families should meet us directly at Hidden Acres Farm at 10:45 AM. Please do not drop off part-time students at the school, as River Tech will not provide transportation for them.
Part-time students are welcome to enjoy the farm alongside their full-time River Tech friends at no admission cost.
Please note:
A parent or designated adult must provide transportation and remain at the farm to supervise their student.
Families must pay for any produce their student picks.
River Tech will cover produce costs only for registered full-time students participating in the Student Farmers Market.
Part-time students may join a River Tech group when accompanied and supervised by their own adult.
When to finish
Homeschool families attend of their own accord. They are welcome to finish when the full-time students finish, or at a time of their own choosing.

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Student devices
sources.content:
Student devices
Choose a device for your student’s grade and program.
You don’t need to replace a working, reliable device that runs your student’s class apps just to buy a newer or more expensive model. Use a supported operating system that receives security updates, and keep it current.
Full-time students and Friday students bring their device daily, charged each evening. Homeschoolers who attend only Monday, Tuesday, and/or Thursday don’t need a device.
Elementary, through 3rd grade
A tablet is all you need.
An iPad from 2022 or newer is recommended; a current Android tablet like the Samsung Galaxy Tab A9+ also works.
At least 64GB of storage (128GB preferred).
Avoid Amazon Fire tablets; they don’t reliably run the apps we use.
4th–6th grade
A laptop is recommended, but a tablet is still fine.
Laptop: an ordinary modern Mac or Windows laptop with enough storage for classwork. 16GB of memory is recommended when buying, but a working, compatible laptop with less is fine; dedicated graphics are not required.
Tablet: an iPad from 2022 or newer is recommended, or a current Android tablet such as the Samsung Galaxy Tab A9+. At least 64GB of storage (128GB preferred). Avoid Amazon Fire tablets.
Full-time 7th–8th grade
An ordinary, reliable modern Mac or Windows laptop is required. It should run the class apps, including Scratch, and have enough storage for classwork. 16GB of memory is recommended when buying, but a working, compatible laptop with less is fine. Dedicated graphics are not required.
Homeschool 7th–12th grade
For classes that need a device, an ordinary, reliable modern Mac or Windows laptop is required. It should run the class apps, including Scratch, and have enough storage for classwork. 16GB of memory is recommended when buying, but a working, compatible laptop with less is fine. Dedicated graphics are not required, even for homeschool high school students.
Homeschool students below 7th grade follow the guidance for their grade above.
Full-time high school, 9th–12th grade
Only full-time high school students need a powerful laptop with these specifications:
Mac: Apple-silicon MacBook, M1 or newer; at least 16GB unified memory; at least 256GB storage (512GB preferred).
Windows: a recent Windows 11 laptop; at least 16GB RAM; dedicated NVIDIA RTX 2050/3050-class graphics or better; at least 256GB SSD (512GB preferred).
For full-time high school, avoid: 8GB RAM configurations, Chromebooks, Intel-based MacBooks, and Windows laptops with only basic integrated graphics.
A refurbished laptop can be a great value from a reputable seller with a clear return policy and warranty. If you’d like, send us a listing before you buy and we’ll confirm the configuration is a good fit. Unsure whether a device is powerful enough? Contact the school at learn@rivertech.me for advice.

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Dress code
sources.content:
Dress code
Modest, professional, distraction-free.
River Tech’s daily-wear standard supports learning, safety, focus, modesty, and professionalism while promoting school identity and parity among students. Our emphasis is on character over appearance (1 Peter 3:3–4). Uniforms are optional; daily wear is flexible within these standards.
Helpful test: would you feel confident sending your student to a job interview in this outfit?
[Image: River Tech dress code visual guide]
Detailed guide
Tops. Collared polos, henleys, blouses, button-downs, knit tops, t-shirts, crewneck/V-neck sweaters, and cardigans. Sleeveless is OK with straps at least 2.5 inches wide and fitted arm openings. Opaque fabrics; necklines stay professional with cleavage covered.
Bottoms. Chinos/khakis, trousers, joggers (P.E. only), and neat denim. Shorts, skirts, skorts, and dresses at fingertip length or longer. Distressing kept refined: any hole no larger than a half-dollar, and never exposing skin above fingertip length.
Coverage & fit. Midriff and seat stay covered during normal activity (walking, sitting, standing, bending, stretching). Garments fit securely at the waist; loose is fine, overly baggy is not. Undergarments stay fully covered.
Footwear. Clean, secure shoes suited to indoor and outdoor movement. Closed-toe shoes are required for labs, shop, and certain field trips. For P.E.: running shoes and athletic socks.
Layers & outerwear. In class: sweaters, cardigans, light jackets, vests, and school-spirit outerwear. Sunglasses, bandanas, scarves, and heavy coats are for arrival, dismissal, and outdoors; store them during class unless needed for health.
Accessories & jewelry. Subtle, safe, and distraction-free. Piercing jewelry in ears only (modest studs or hoops). No spikes, sharp hardware, or unsafe accessories. Belts, watches, and simple bracelets/necklaces are welcome when subtle and safe.
Hair & grooming. Clean, neat, and professional. No carved names, symbols, or numbers. One natural hair color; natural-colored highlights and lowlights are allowed. Facial hair neatly trimmed.
Makeup & nails. Moderate and well-kept, suited to a professional and educational setting.
Graphics, messages & symbols. Allowed when school-appropriate and aligned with River Tech values. Not allowed: violence, drugs/alcohol/tobacco, profanity, sexual content, or demeaning themes.
P.E. & active wear. Required: running shoes; athletic shorts, sweats, or joggers; an athletic top. Length and coverage standards still apply. Tie back long hair for safety.
Enforcement
An isolated dress correction is a minor violation; handled quietly by the teacher with an on-the-spot fix where possible. Repeated disregard becomes a pattern concern and moves to an administrative response.

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Does River Tech offer transportation or bus service?+
sources.content:
Does River Tech offer transportation or bus service?+
River Tech does not operate a daily bus route for drop-off or pick-up. Families drop off and pick up students directly at our campus at 927 E Polston Ave in Post Falls. That said, we do operate a school bus and a school van for weekly park trips and for field trips, so your student still gets to ride with their class when we head out for the day. Because most of our families are within a short drive of campus, many parents also organize informal carpools with other River Tech families in their neighborhood.

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · What is River Tech School?
sources.content:
What is River Tech School?
River Tech School is a private Christian school of Performing Arts and Technology in Post Falls, Idaho, serving grades 1 through 12. We keep classes small, around 15 students each, and we integrate performing arts and technology with core academics inside a Christian worldview. River Tech is operated by Faithful Five Inc., an Idaho nonprofit corporation, and we enroll both full-time students and homeschool families who want one to four days per week of enrichment.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · What is River Tech School?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Is River Tech a Christian school?
sources.content:
Is River Tech a Christian school?
Yes. River Tech is a Christian school, and our faith is woven through the entire day rather than isolated to a single Bible class. Each day begins with prayer, worship, and gratitude. We do not promote one denomination over another. Instead, we follow C.S. Lewis’s “mere Christianity” principle of sticking to the fundamentals of the faith and leaving the finer details of doctrine to families and their churches. Our teachers are Christians, and our parent organization, Faithful Five Inc., is an Idaho nonprofit corporation founded on Christian principles.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · Is River Tech a Christian school?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Is River Tech a full-time school or a homeschool enrichment program?
sources.content:
Is River Tech a full-time school or a homeschool enrichment program?
River Tech is a full-time school that also offers flexible homeschool programs. Homeschool students may enroll in 1–4 days per week and participate in select classes alongside our full-time students, depending on availability.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · Is River Tech a full-time school or a homeschool enrichment program?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Can homeschool families use River Tech part-time?
sources.content:
Can homeschool families use River Tech part-time?
Yes. River Tech offers an à la carte program for homeschool families who want one to four days per week of enrichment. You can choose Monday Performing Arts, Tuesday Science and Social Studies, Thursday Life Skills, Friday Technology, or any combination of them. This lets homeschool parents keep the home-based core of their week while giving their child specialized instruction, community, and hands-on facilities they cannot easily replicate at home. Homeschool families are welcome to join most of our field trip and workshop days, which happen about every three weeks. Each trip has its own sign-up, and some carry a cost depending on the activity. Many of our homeschoolers tell us this is one of their favorite parts of the program.

sources.content:
What grades do you serve, and what are class sizes like?
River Tech serves students in 1st through 12th grade. Class sizes vary by subject:
Music and foreign language classes typically have around 7 students.
Core subjects such as Math, English, and Science average 10–15 students.
Group-based classes like coding or choir may include up to 20 students, in which case two teachers are present.
Overall, River Tech maintains an effective 1:15 teacher–student ratio, allowing for personalized learning and strong teacher–student relationships.

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · What does a typical week look like at River Tech?
sources.content:
What does a typical week look like at River Tech?
A typical week at River Tech blends core academics with performing arts, technology, and life skills each day. Mondays focus on performing arts, including music, theater, and dance. Tuesdays lean into science and social studies. Wednesdays are a full academic day. Thursdays are built around life skills, biblical worldview, and community. Fridays are our technology day, covering coding, robotics, filmmaking, and digital design. Every day begins with prayer, worship, and gratitude, and every day includes math, reading, and writing appropriate to the student’s level.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · What does a typical week look like at River Tech?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · How does competency-based learning work at River Tech?
sources.content:
How does competency-based learning work at River Tech?
Competency-based learning means students progress when they have mastered the material, not when the calendar says so. At River Tech, a third-grade student who is ready for fifth-grade math is placed in fifth-grade math, and a student who needs more time in reading gets it without being labeled or held back. Teachers track progress against clear competencies, and students move up a level in each subject as they demonstrate they are ready. The result is that no student is bored because the class is too slow, and no student is lost because the class is too fast.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · How does competency-based learning work at River Tech?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · What is River Tech’s culture like?
sources.content:
What is River Tech’s culture like?
Each day here begins with prayer, worship, and gratitude, not as an add-on, but as the foundation everything else rests on. We teach children to love God and their families, honor their community and country, take personal responsibility, earn what they achieve, and build something of their own. We do not teach gender ideology, critical race theory, victim mentality, or cancel culture.

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · How does River Tech handle physical fitness and sports?
sources.content:
How does River Tech handle physical fitness and sports?
Physical activity is built into every week at River Tech. Students spend about twenty minutes each day on drill and calisthenics, which teaches focus, posture, and the discipline of moving as a group while building real physical readiness. Once a week we head to the park for additional physical education, and every three weeks or so we take a field trip that is often physically active, such as wall climbing, trampoline jumping, or roller skating. At River Tech we teach sportsmanship, mobility, and mental toughness through athletics and fitness training because, in the words of Paul, “your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit” (1 Cor 6:19-20).
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · How does River Tech handle physical fitness and sports?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · How is River Tech different from a traditional private school?
sources.content:
How is River Tech different from a traditional private school?
River Tech differs from a traditional private school in many ways. Here are three examples. First, we are an openly Christian school. Each day begins with prayer, worship, and gratitude, and faith is woven through everything we teach. Second, we specialize in performing arts and technology, which means students are taught musical theater, dance, and instruments alongside coding, robotics, and filmmaking. Third, we have an unusually strong school culture. We hold regular assemblies, take weekly park trips, run field trips every three weeks, and throw wholesome school parties together, which builds the kind of community that is hard to find in bigger schools.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · How is River Tech different from a traditional private school?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Is River Tech accredited?
sources.content:
Is River Tech accredited?
River Tech is currently unaccredited and issues its own diplomas and transcripts. Ask the school about current accreditation plans and any requirements relevant to your student’s next step.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · Is River Tech accredited?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Do River Tech graduates get a real high school diploma?
sources.content:
Do River Tech graduates get a real high school diploma?
Yes. Long gone are the days when colleges looked down on homeschool families and small private schools. Today most colleges actually welcome students like ours with open hearts, because the competency, initiative, and values of these students tend to be well-suited to college life. River Tech has several students who are already taking college courses while enrolled with us, and they have run into no obstacles along the way. We issue a formal diploma and transcript, all of our teachers hold degrees (in most cases multiple degrees), and we teach the subjects colleges actually care about. One example is our annual essay. Where most high schools assign one capstone project in the senior year, every River Tech student writes a full college-thesis-style essay every year, complete with references, footnotes, and the structural rigor colleges expect. By the time a River Tech student graduates, they have written four or more of these, not one.

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Managing your payments.
sources.content:
Managing your payments.
Your invoice
Invoices arrive through FreshBooks from Faithful Five, River Tech’s nonprofit ministry. Quarterly billing is the standard plan. You can set up automatic payments through your invoice.
Paying by check
Checks are accepted on quarterly and annual plans only. If you currently pay monthly by check, switch to a quarterly or annual plan to continue using checks, or pay your monthly invoice by card or bank transfer.
Withdrawals & tuition refunds
Tuition is calculated by calendar month, not by individual classes or days attended.
Monthly payments: Families may withdraw and stop paying the next month’s tuition. A month that has begun is not prorated or refunded.
Quarterly or annual payments: Prepaid months that have not begun are refundable. A month that has begun is not prorated or refunded.
Please contact learn@rivertech.me to arrange a withdrawal.
Need a different arrangement?
If you’re using the Idaho Parental Choice Tax Credit or need to discuss your payment plan, contact us.
How much does River Tech cost?
Tuition for the 2026-27 school year depends on how many days per week your child attends and which payment plan you choose. On our standard quarterly plan, 5-day full-time school is $1,950 per quarter ($7,800 per year), and 4-day full-time school is $1,679 per quarter ($6,716 per year). À la carte homeschool enrichment is $365 per quarter for one day per week, $690 for two days, $960 for three days, and $1,199 for four days. Monthly and annual payment plans are also available, and our Tuition page has the full table. There is also a one-time household enrollment fee of $250, due when a seat is offered from the wait pool and accepted. A sibling discount is available for families with multiple children enrolled. Idaho families may qualify for the Parental Choice Tax Credit, which can offset a meaningful portion of tuition.
Where can I find scholarship information?
River Tech is at full capacity and is not accepting scholarship applications. Join our free wait pool and indicate whether your child would need a River Tech scholarship to attend.

sources.content:
Is enrollment open?
River Tech is at full capacity — about 130 students — so there is no open enrollment period. But seats do open: we expect room for a few new students in January, and more each fall as students graduate. All of them are filled from our wait pool — you can join it here.

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Do you accept new students mid-year?
sources.content:
Do you accept new students mid-year?
Yes — when a seat is open. January, after Christmas break, is the most common mid-year starting point. Wait pool families hear first. If your family is new to the area or in an unusual situation, write to learn@rivertech.me — we read everything.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · Do you accept new students mid-year?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · How does the wait pool work?
sources.content:
How does the wait pool work?
One free form, no commitment. When a seat opens in your child’s grade, we look for the child who fits that class — a school built around performing arts and technology serves children who want to sing, act, build, and code. While you wait, you’re invited to River Tech Days and our productions, so the school isn’t a stranger when we call.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · How does the wait pool work?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · How long is the wait?
sources.content:
How long is the wait?
We don’t know, and we won’t guess at your expense. Some grades turn over a seat or two a year; some don’t. What we can promise: we’ll be straight with you about where things stand, and if you’ve made other plans, just tell us — we’d rather know than hold a place you no longer need.
sources.keywords: Family Hub | River Tech · How long is the wait?

sources.title: Family Hub | River Tech · Why not expand?
sources.content:
Why not expand?
Because the size is what makes the school work. At about 130 students, every teacher knows every child. Growing past our walls and our ratios would seat more families at the cost of the thing they came for. If a larger permanent home comes someday, we’ll revisit it. Until then, full means full.

Faithful Five
501(c)(3) Nonprofit
We’re glad you’re here! Faithful Five started as a simple family dream: a mom, dad, and their three kids wanting to make a difference. Today, we’re a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a dedicated board of caring individuals. We run River Tech School, where students thrive through personalized learning, and extend compassion to our community through the Jesus People Coffee House, a welcoming space offering support and resources to those experiencing homelessness.
Our mission is to strengthen lives through faith-based education and genuine outreach. Join us in building a stronger, more compassionate community.

sources.title: Faithful Five: 501(c)(3) Nonprofit | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls, ID · Our Journey and Mission
sources.content:
Our Journey and Mission
It all began around our family kitchen table. Dan, Mary, and our three children felt a deep calling to serve others in meaningful ways. What was once a family dream has grown into Faithful Five, a nonprofit run by a handful of dedicated board members who share our passion for making a positive impact.
River Tech School is our primary work. As a 1–12 Christian school, we focus on personalized learning and small class sizes so each student’s gifts can be seen and developed. By integrating technology and the performing arts with core academics, we are preparing the next generation of creative thinkers and leaders, and our commitment extends beyond the classroom.
Through the Jesus People Coffee House, led by Linda Meissner from the pages of David Wilkerson’s book The Cross and the Switchblade, we reach out to those experiencing homelessness. Offering free coffee, food, clothing, and Christian support, we aim to meet immediate needs while also helping individuals find pathways to rehabilitation and renewed hope.
[Image: River Tech - Nonprofit]
We’re a community built on kindness, faith, and service. Our board and team operate with transparency and integrity, making sure every effort moves our mission forward.

sources.content:
Idaho Roots
River Tech reflects the character of our region. Idaho runs on faith, family, hard work, and time spent outdoors, and so do we. Kids grow best when school and home share the same direction, and we want parents to know ours before they enroll.
sources.keywords: Our Culture | River Tech · Idaho Roots

sources.title: Our Culture | River Tech · A Christian School
sources.content:
A Christian School
Our staff are Christians, and the shape of the school day reflects that. We open each morning with worship, prayer, and a short devotional. Faith runs through the day rather than being set aside during classes.
We welcome families from many different churches, and we don't promote one denomination over another. C.S. Lewis had a phrase for this: “mere Christianity,” a shared foundation that honors the core of the faith while leaving the details to churches and parents.
[Image: The River Tech teaching team]
sources.keywords: Our Culture | River Tech · A Christian School

sources.title: Our Culture | River Tech · A Small School, on Purpose
sources.content:
A Small School, on Purpose
Our classes are small, about fifteen students, because that's the size where a school can actually know a child. Every teacher knows every student by name, knows what they're working on, and notices when something is off. We lean on parents, too, for volunteer days, guest teaching, field-trip help, and honest feedback about what's working and what isn't. River Tech is a community, and your family is part of it.
sources.keywords: Our Culture | River Tech · A Small School, on Purpose

sources.title: Our Culture | River Tech · What We Stand For, and What We Don't
sources.content:
What We Stand For, and What We Don't
We stand for God, family, church, community, personal responsibility, patriotism, merit, grit, and entrepreneurship.
We don't teach gender ideology, critical race theory, victim mentality, or cancel culture. We are committed instead to a stable, time-tested framework that fosters character, strength, clarity, and wisdom.
Students are addressed as boys and girls. Our teachers prepare students for adult life, including courtship, marriage, and parenting. But our students do not engage in idle talk about crushes, romantic relationships, or LGBTQ.
sources.keywords: Our Culture | River Tech · What We Stand For, and What We Don't

sources.title: Our Culture | River Tech · Grit
sources.content:
Grit
Kids need challenge to become capable adults. A child should never experience abuse, harm, or bullying, but they should absolutely experience discomfort, frustration, and the feeling of something genuinely hard, in order to become resilient under pressure.
We spend about twenty minutes each day on drill and calisthenics. Drill teaches focus, posture, and the discipline of moving as a group. Calisthenics builds real physical readiness. Once a week we head to the park, and every three weeks or so we take a field trip, often something physical like wall climbing, trampoline jumping, or roller skating. We celebrate the wins, too, from birthdays and finished projects to end-of-term parties and the kind of everyday moments that make kids feel at home.
[Image: River Tech students climbing at a bouldering gym on a field trip]
sources.keywords: Our Culture | River Tech · Grit

sources.title: Our Culture | River Tech · Real Life Before Digital Life
sources.content:
Real Life Before Digital Life
We're a technology school, but we believe real-life experiences are foundational for healthy growth. That's why we balance tech classes with performing arts, liberal arts, and life skills, and that's why we protect the things technology can't replace: family time, real friendships, time in nature, creative work, and a growing faith.
sources.keywords: Our Culture | River Tech · Real Life Before Digital Life

sources.title: Our Culture | River Tech · How We Teach Hard Things
sources.content:
How We Teach Hard Things
Our classrooms take on the great stories, histories, and ideas of the world, including the difficult ones. War, mythology, and competing worldviews are central to understanding the human story, and we don't flinch from them. We teach them with Christian commentary and a conservative frame, so that students come away with moral clarity rather than moral confusion.
sources.keywords: Our Culture | River Tech · How We Teach Hard Things

sources.title: Our Culture | River Tech · If You've Read This Far
sources.content:
If You've Read This Far
If this sounds like home, we'd love to meet your family. Come by for a tour, sit in on morning worship and a class or two, and see for yourself whether your child would be at home here. If it sounds like a mismatch, we respect that and wish you well. Our goal is that every family finds the right fit, and that you have clarity about that from the beginning. Reach out; we would love to hear from you.

sources.title: Performing Arts Program | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls · Performing Arts
sources.content:
Performing Arts
The Performing Arts live at the very heart of River Tech's identity. Music, drama, and dance awaken creativity, discipline, and joy in students, shaping both their character and their confidence. Through the arts, they learn to tell stories that matter, to move hearts, and to bring beauty into a world that desperately needs it.
At River Tech, we see artistic expression as a calling, an opportunity to reflect the creativity of the Creator. Every rehearsal, every performance, every note sung or line spoken is a step toward mastering both craft and spirit.
"Sing to him a new song; play skillfully on the strings, with loud shouts." – Psalm 33:3 ESV
Just as athletics trains the body and technology sharpens the mind, the arts shape the soul. Students discover the power of teamwork, perseverance, and imagination, developing gifts that will serve them in every area of life. Our vision is to raise up a generation that can move audiences, heal hearts, and glorify God through their creative expression.
Join us as we raise performers who shine with excellence, courage, and wonder, artists prepared for the stage and for every stage of life.
Meet Our Teachers
MUSICALS
Our annual musicals are a celebration of talent, teamwork, and imagination. Every week, students rehearse singing, dancing, and acting, while a behind-the-scenes crew brings the magic to life with props, sets, and lighting. Open to anyone willing to audition and commit, each musical challenges students to push their skills further. Productions get bigger, bolder, and more spectacular each year. From the first rehearsal to the final curtain call, River Tech musicals are where creativity soars and every student has a chance to shine.
[Image: River Tech students performing in a musical on stage]

June, 2023: The Lion King
"The Lion King" at River Tech
River Tech's production of "The Lion King" set a new standard for our musicals. This ambitious rendition featured 16 lapel microphones for crystal-clear audio and two full bands, adding rich, immersive depth to the musical score.
Our students took on advanced dance routines that brought the world of the savannah to life on stage. The extended script gave our actors more space to develop their characters and connect with the audience.
Daenerys deserves special recognition for her role as Timba. Her comedic timing and expressive performance had the audience erupting in laughter, making her portrayal a standout highlight of the show.

"Annie" at River Tech

Our students shone brightly, embracing the rhythmic dance numbers with enthusiasm and skill. The live band added a dynamic layer to the show, filling the auditorium with energy and excitement.
We also introduced lapel microphones for this production, giving our actors' voices greater clarity and reach.
"Annie" was a journey of growth for River Tech. Each song, dance, and line delivered by our talented students reflected their dedication and passion, making "Annie" a memorable and inspiring experience for our school community.

sources.title: Technology Program | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls, ID · Technology
sources.content:
Technology
The Technology branch at River Tech is where innovation and wisdom meet. Coding, robotics, engineering, and digital design are tools for building and stewarding God's world with excellence. Technology sharpens the mind, teaches problem-solving, and prepares students to shape the future rather than be shaped by it.
[Image: River Tech - Technology]
At River Tech, we see technology as more than gadgets and screens. It is a calling to create, to innovate, and to bring order out of complexity. Every program written, every circuit connected, every prototype designed is an opportunity to reflect the brilliance of the Creator, who formed all things with precision and purpose.
"Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men." – Colossians 3:23 ESV
Just as athletics trains the body and the arts shape the soul, technology strengthens the mind. Students learn perseverance in debugging, creativity in design, and discipline in engineering. Our vision is to raise up a generation that doesn't just consume technology but builds it, wields it responsibly, and glorifies God through innovation.
Join us as we raise up inventors, builders, and problem-solvers who will bring excellence, courage, and ingenuity to every area of life.
Sincerely, / Jordan Ezell / Technology Director
Meet Our Teachers
CODING
At River Tech, coding is more than a skill. It's a journey of discovery, creativity, and balance. We equip students with tools to thrive in a world shaped by technology, while helping them grow as well-rounded people grounded in Christian values and enriched by the arts. With screen-free Wednesdays and structured coding sessions, we promote a healthy relationship with technology.
sources.keywords: Technology Program | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls, ID · Technology

sources.title: Technology Program | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls, ID · Technology
sources.content:
Our coding curriculum begins in second grade with Scratch Jr., building logical thinking and problem-solving in a playful, approachable way. As students advance, they transition from Scratch into text-based languages like Python and C#, using platforms such as Unity to design games and apps. This progression develops coding proficiency along with creativity and resilience.
Beyond coding, River Tech integrates performing arts, crafts, life skills, and faith, preparing students to meet tomorrow's challenges as both skilled coders and thoughtful leaders shaped by wisdom, integrity, and imagination.
sources.keywords: Technology Program | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls, ID · Technology

sources.title: Technology Program | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls, ID · Coding Curriculum Progression
sources.content:
Coding Curriculum Progression
Scratch Jr. (2nd grade) → Scratch (block-based coding) → Python → C# with Unity (game & app development)
ROBOTICS
Our robotics program takes students on a hands-on journey of discovery, beginning as early as second grade. Using the Vex Robotics curriculum, students learn the fundamentals of mechanical design by working with gears, shafts, standoffs, and other components to build robotic arms, cars, and Ferris wheels. This foundation builds both creativity and technical understanding as students see how individual parts come together to form working machines.
From there, they bring their creations to life through coding, discovering the relationship between software and hardware. As their skills grow, students tackle Vex Go competitions that mirror real-world challenges, from ocean exploration to city infrastructure and even Mars missions. These projects emphasize teamwork, problem-solving, and innovation over competition alone. Students then advance to Arduino, deepening their robotics knowledge through open-source programming and more complex applications. Our program equips students with the technical expertise and critical thinking skills needed to lead in tomorrow's world of technology and engineering.
sources.keywords: Technology Program | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls, ID · Coding Curriculum Progression

sources.title: Technology Program | River Tech Christian School | Post Falls, ID · Robotics Curriculum Progression
sources.content:

Vex Robotics (foundational) → Arduino (advanced projects)
3D DESIGN
Our 3D modeling program introduces students to digital creation through Blender. From designing characters and environments to producing animations and 3D prints, students gain hands-on experience that unlocks the creative, technical, and spatial parts of the mind.
Each week, they learn new techniques: shaping objects, adding textures, lighting scenes, and animating movement, steadily building confidence in their skills. Over time, students also learn to prepare and print their own models, connecting the digital to the physical.
Our program equips students with the imagination and technical skills to thrive in the growing fields of digital media, animation, and design.

sources.title: Why River Tech? | Christian School in Post Falls, ID · Why Choose River Tech?
sources.content:
Why Choose River Tech?
At River Tech each child learns at their own pace.
River Tech is built for artistic and tech-savvy kids who love music and technology. Along with core subjects (Math, Language Arts, Social Science, and Science), students learn technology (coding, robotics, filmmaking, and digital arts) and performing arts (music, band, choir, acting, dance, and musical theater).
Grounded in Christian values and a family-centered culture, students receive the social and academic foundation they need to succeed in life. With class sizes around 15 students, roughly half that of public schools, our teachers spend more time with each student. Through competency-based learning, each student moves at their own pace while enjoying the benefits of a positive social environment.
A student begins at a given competency level and moves to the next when they've mastered it. This competency-based approach guides each student’s progress through the material. Students receive grades for their work while learning at a pace suited to their understanding.
If a student excels at a subject, they can move faster. If a subject is harder, they can take more time. A child can be at different levels in different tracks.
Read a brief summary of our highlights below. For full curriculum details, click 'view more' under any track.
[Image: Students building robots at River Tech]
TECHNOLOGY
River Tech is a School of Technology. Students learn coding, digital arts, 3D modeling, robotics, filmmaking, digital design, Legos, engineering, and more.
This track is hands-on: learning by doing, building projects, and playing.

Bible Syllabus — High School
2026–2027
INSTRUCTOR INFORMATION
Instructor Email Room Location & Hours
Kirsten Decker Kirsten@rivertech.me Dance Hall — Fridays, 1:00-1:40 PM
GENERAL INFORMATION
Description
This course walks 9th–12th graders through Scripture using different reflection methods each quarter: Lectio
Divina/One Word, S.O.A.P. Devotional, Character Study/POV Rewrites of major biblical figures, and a Biggest
Lie / Biggest Truth study that pushes back against cultural lies with Scripture. The goal is to build a mature,
personal habit of engaging with the Bible through different devotionals.
Expectations and Goals
Students are expected to bring their Bible and journal to class each week, complete that week's reflection using
the assigned method, and participate in class discussion. By the end of the year, students should be able to
apply four different methods of Scripture engagement, write from another person's perspective with empathy
and insight, and articulate how Scripture speaks against cultural lies.
COURSE MATERIALS
Required Materials
• A Bible (any translation)
• A journal or notebook dedicated to weekly reflections
• A pen or pencil
Optional Materials
• Colored pens or highlighters for journaling
Required Text
The Bible — translation of the student/family's choice

High School Chemistry Syllabus
Course Title
High School Chemistry
Grade Level
Grades 9–12
Course Length
Full academic year
Credit
1 high-school science credit upon successful completion, subject to school graduation
requirements.
Course Description
High School Chemistry is a teacher-directed, laboratory-based course examining matter and its
interactions at the atomic, molecular, and macroscopic levels.
All students will progress through the curriculum together according to a common course
schedule.
Students will use Barron’s Visual Learning: Chemistry as the primary conceptual text.
Teacher-created supplemental instruction will provide the mathematical skills, worked
examples, practice problems, laboratory analysis, and additional content necessary for a
complete high-school chemistry course.
Major topics include measurement, atomic structure, the periodic table, chemical bonding,
molecular structure, chemical nomenclature, reactions, moles, stoichiometry, solutions, acids
and bases, gases, thermochemistry, reaction rates, equilibrium, oxidation-reduction, and
nuclear chemistry.
The course emphasizes direct instruction, mathematical problem solving, scientific reasoning,
laboratory investigation, and cumulative understanding.
Primary Resource

Course Format
This is a traditional teacher-paced course.
Students will:
● Study the same material at the same time.
● Follow a common unit schedule.
● Complete the same core assignments.
● Participate in scheduled class laboratories.
● Complete quizzes and tests on established dates.
● Meet common assignment deadlines.
● Move through the course as a class rather than independently.
Additional help or practice may be provided to students who need it, but the overall class pacing
will remain common.
Students who are absent are responsible for making up missed instruction, assignments, labs,
and assessments according to school policy.
Prerequisites
Students should have working knowledge of:
● Arithmetic
● Fractions
● Decimals
● Percentages
● Ratios and proportions
● Basic algebraic manipulation
Completion of or concurrent enrollment in Algebra I is recommended.

Course Objectives
Upon successful completion of the course, students should be able to:
● Use appropriate scientific measurements and units.
● Apply scientific notation.
● Apply significant figures.
● Perform dimensional analysis.
● Calculate density.
● Describe atomic structure.
● Interpret isotope notation.
● Calculate average atomic mass.
● Explain electron arrangement and periodic trends.
● Predict common ionic charges.
● Write and name ionic and molecular compounds.
● Construct basic Lewis structures.
● Apply VSEPR theory.
● Determine basic molecular polarity.
● Explain intermolecular forces.
● Interpret and balance chemical equations.
● Classify major reaction types.
● Calculate molar mass.
● Convert among mass, moles, and particles.
● Solve stoichiometric problems.
● Identify limiting reactants.
● Calculate theoretical and percent yield.
● Calculate solution concentration.
● Apply molarity and dilution relationships.
● Explain acid-base chemistry.
● Perform introductory pH calculations.
● Analyze a basic titration.
● Apply major gas-law relationships.
● Analyze heat transfer using specific heat and calorimetry.
● Explain endothermic and exothermic processes.
● Describe factors affecting reaction rates.
● Explain activation energy and catalysis.
● Describe chemical equilibrium.
● Apply introductory Le Châtelier reasoning.
● Identify basic oxidation-reduction processes.
● Explain basic nuclear decay and half-life.
● Collect and analyze laboratory data.
● Evaluate experimental error.
● Support conclusions with evidence and calculations.

Homework and Practice
Students should expect regular chemistry practice.
Assignments may include:
● Reading
● Guided notes
● Problem sets
● Calculations
● Vocabulary
● Written explanations
● Lab preparation
● Lab analysis
● Review assignments
Chemistry requires regular practice, particularly in quantitative units.
Assignments will have common due dates.
Laboratory Program
Students will complete selected laboratory investigations as a class throughout the year.
Possible investigations include:
● Density and measurement
● Separation of mixtures
● Solubility and polarity
● Conservation of mass
● Reaction rate
● Acid-base chemistry
● Calorimetry
● Stoichiometry and percent yield
● Titration
● Gas behavior
Laboratory activities may be replaced with demonstrations or simulations when necessary for
safety, equipment limitations, or instructional effectiveness.
Laboratory Reports
Depending on the investigation, students may be required to include:
● Purpose
● Hypothesis or prediction

Not every laboratory activity will require a complete formal report.
Assessment
Students may be evaluated through:
● Homework
● Classwork
● Problem sets
● Quizzes
● Unit tests
● Laboratory work
● Laboratory reports
● Projects
● Quarter assessments
● Cumulative final examination
Grading Policies
Quarterly grades are derived from two distinct components: Academic Performance
(evaluated assignments) and Participation (teacher-assessed engagement and preparation).
While most courses utilize an equal 50/50 weighting, specific courses may be designated as
Skill-Heavy (60/40) or Participation-Heavy (40/60) at the teacher's discretion.
The Academic component is calculated by converting each assignment into a percentage and a
corresponding letter grade. This figure represents a combination of the overall quarterly trend
(60%) and the average of the five most recent assignments (40%). This structure ensures that
student improvement in the latter half of the quarter significantly influences the final grade.
Every assessment carries equal weight within the grading system. Small quizzes and major
projects exert the same influence on the final average, emphasizing the importance of
consistent performance over any individual result.
Grades are recorded using a letter-based system where percentages are snapped to
established midpoints. Consequently, numerical differences within the same letter-band (such
as 84% and 86%) result in the same grade. Students should focus on achieving higher letter-
bands rather than individual points.

sources.title: chemistry-high-school.pdf · page 9
sources.content:
Missing assignments will be recorded as a zero after the designated grace period. Until that
time, the displayed grade only reflects completed work, which may not accurately represent a
student's current academic standing.
Grading Scale: A+ 97–100 · A 93–96 · A− 90–92 · B+ 87–89 · B 83–86 · B− 80–82 · C+ 77–79 · C 73–76 ·
C− 70–72 · D+ 67–69 · D 63–66 · D− 60–62 · F below 60
The final year grade is weighted: Q1 20%, Q2 25%, Q3 25%, and Q4 30%. Cumulative GPA is
calculated on a 4.3 scale, with an A+ representing a 4.3.
Tests and Quizzes
Quizzes will normally assess material recently taught.
Each major unit will generally conclude with a test or other formal assessment.
Major assessments may include material from earlier portions of the course because chemistry
concepts build upon one another.
Students will normally receive structured review before major tests.
Mathematics Expectations
High-school chemistry requires students to show their mathematical reasoning.
Unless otherwise directed, calculations should include:
1. Appropriate formula or relationship
2. Given information
3. Substitution
4. Units
5. Mathematical work
6. Final answer
Answers without supporting work may receive reduced credit.
Scientific calculators may be used when permitted by the teacher.
Laboratory Safety
Students must:
● Follow teacher instructions at all times.
● Wear required protective equipment.
● Use chemicals only as directed.

Grading Policies
Quarterly grades are derived from two distinct components: Academic Performance
(evaluated assignments) and Participation (teacher-assessed engagement and preparation).
While most courses utilize an equal 50/50 weighting, specific courses may be designated as
Skill-Heavy (60/40) or Participation-Heavy (40/60) at the teacher's discretion.
The Academic component is calculated by converting each assignment into a percentage and a
corresponding letter grade. This figure represents a combination of the overall quarterly trend
(60%) and the average of the five most recent assignments (40%). This structure ensures that
student improvement in the latter half of the quarter significantly influences the final grade.
Every assessment carries equal weight within the grading system. Small quizzes and major
projects exert the same influence on the final average, emphasizing the importance of
consistent performance over any individual result.
Grades are recorded using a letter-based system where percentages are snapped to
established midpoints. Consequently, numerical differences within the same letter-band (such
as 84% and 86%) result in the same grade. Students should focus on achieving higher letter-
bands rather than individual points.
Missing assignments will be recorded as a zero after the designated grace period. Until that
time, the displayed grade only reflects completed work, which may not accurately represent a
student's current academic standing.
Grading Scale: A+ 97–100 · A 93–96 · A− 90–92 · B+ 87–89 · B 83–86 · B− 80–82 · C+ 77–79 · C 73–76 ·

GENERAL INFORMATION
Description
The goal of this class is not to cover a filmmaking curriculum. The goal is to make filmmaking fun enough that students keep
filming at home, and then to keep giving them tools, challenges, and reasons to do it.
How a Week Runs
Two formats alternate, along with the ongoing quarter project:
• Shoot week: 5 min watching student films from the screening queue, 5 min inspiration clip and intro, 25 min shooting,
5 min quick edit and watch.
• Edit week: 5 min watching student clips, 35 min editing and watching last week's film, with extra time spent teaching
editing technique.
The class shoots as one group with Mr. Luke directing. There are no assigned crew roles — everyone is on camera, and
helper jobs are volunteered. All class footage is cut on Mr. Luke's laptop and projected, with a student driving; nothing
transfers to student devices.
Expectations and Goals
Students are expected to participate fully in the weekly in-class shoot or edit, and are encouraged (though not required
beyond a floor of two submissions per quarter) to film short films at home with friends and family. Every week ends with
one home challenge that can be done on a phone.
COURSE MATERIALS
Required Materials
• CapCut (free) — the class default, set up together in Week 1
• A phone or tablet for home filming (school equipment is used for in-class shoots)
Optional Materials
• iMovie or Clipchamp — fallback editors if CapCut isn't available

The Q2 film project is made from Part One of the hero's journey story each student writes in English during Q1. Each

Leadership Mindset Syllabus
High School

INSTRUCTOR INFORMATION
Instructor Email Room Location & Hours
Penny Burciaga Penny@rivertech.me The Café — Tuesdays, 11:05–11:45
AM
GENERAL INFORMATION
Course Summary
Leadership Mindset is grounded in Scripture and is a 35-week course that teaches students to lead from a fixed
external standard (Scripture) and to reason with the models real organizations use. The first semester
establishes twelve leadership principles shaping mindsets, each given a technical definition, anchored in
Scripture, and demonstrated by a named biblical leader. The second semester introduces twenty-one mental
models drawn from Toyota, military strategy, systems theory, behavioral economics, and value investing, each
paired with the scriptural principle that governs its use. The two semesters answer two different questions:
what standard governs this decision, and what tool structures the analysis.
Note: modifications may be made to accommodate school needs. Breadth and depth of content may be adjusted
depending on demonstrated competency of learning objectives.
How the Course Is Taught
The course runs on a roughly 95% activity / 5% instruction model, consistent with the school's hands-on mission.
In each 30-minute session a concept is framed in two to three minutes, students spend the bulk of the time
performing it, and the learning is consolidated in a short debrief. Concepts are discovered through the activity
rather than delivered before it; students hit a vague ask, a blown estimate, or a defensive reaction first, and
name the principle afterward. Every session opens with two minutes on who applied last week's principle and
sources.keywords: leadership-high-school.pdf · page 1

sources.title: leadership-high-school.pdf · page 1
sources.content:
what resulted, which is the primary retention mechanism available in a once-weekly format.
Why Principles Precede Models
Leadership content commonly teaches technique and assumes character will follow. This course reverses the
order. Semester One is taught as behavior with observable repetitions rather than as values to be discussed, so a
student is measured on whether the behavior was performed. Semester Two then supplies the analytical tools,
and Week 19 states the distinction to students directly: a model is an instrument for judgment, not a substitute
for it, and no model carries the authority the standard carries.

sources.title: leadership-high-school.pdf · page 2
sources.content:
Rivertech School 2026/2027
River Tech School  •  Life is a Stage. Love is our Script.  •  Page 2
Biblical Integration
Scripture is integrated at the point of concept rather than appended as devotional framing, and is quoted from
the NKJV. Every principle and every model carries a scriptural anchor and a named biblical leader who
demonstrates it, so students learn the standard and the exemplar together. Models are taught for their
mechanics rather than as endorsements of the leaders or companies associated with them, and this is stated to
students directly in the bridge session.
Coverage
The curriculum is mapped against the full range of leadership competencies, so no core discipline is missed.
Conflict receives four weeks because it carries nine sub-topics and is the one area where students reliably bring
live material. Secondary skills, including public speaking mechanics, meeting facilitation, and written brevity, are
addressed through embedded repetitions inside later units and the capstone defense, giving honest coverage
without inflating the calendar. Two of the 35 weeks are protected as float to absorb schedule loss from other
school activities.
Relationship to the Organizational Design & Management Course
Some students take the parallel Organizational Design & Management course, which builds a collective system:
what happens when individually-led people must build a structure, culture, and management system together.
This course is the individual counterpart, meaning the standard and the reasoning a person brings into any
structure. Frameworks shared between the two, including root cause analysis, bottleneck identification, and
retrospectives, function here as primary instruction and there as reinforcement in a new context. The course
stands fully on its own.

COURSE MATERIALS
Required Materials
• A Bible — Scripture is quoted from the NKJV in class
• A notebook for weekly artifacts and objectives
ASSESSMENT
Assessment is performance-based and behavioral. Students are evaluated on observable conduct rather than on
personal disclosure, and no reflection on feelings is graded. Artifacts include a structured request, a written
conflict-resolution sequence, a root cause analysis, a pre-mortem, a constraint diagnosis, and a bias audit.
The capstone requires each student to present an unresolved problem from their own experience, name the
principle that governs the decision and the model that structures the analysis, and defend both selections
against challenge from the room. Students are assessed on whether the correct tool was selected and applied
accurately, not on whether the problem was solved.

Organizational Design & Management Syllabus
High School
2026–2027
INSTRUCTOR INFORMATION
Instructor Email Room Location & Hours
Penny Burciaga Penny@rivertech.me The Café — Tuesdays, 10:25–11:05 AM
GENERAL INFORMATION
Course Summary
Organizational Design & Management is a 35-week course that teaches students how real organizations are built and run by
having them build and run one. Working in teams, students found an invented company in Week 4 and develop it
continuously across every functional area of a business, from legal formation and governance through funding, structure,
people, operations, marketing, sales, finance, legal protection, and change. This running company is the spine of the course:
it turns 35 otherwise-separate topics into one continuous, real-world experience.
Note: modifications may be made to accommodate school needs. Breadth and depth of content may be adjusted depending
on demonstrated competency of learning objectives.
How the Course Is Taught
The course runs on a roughly 95% activity / 5% instruction model, consistent with the school's hands-on mission. In each 30-
minute session, a concept is framed in two to three minutes, students spend the bulk of the time doing, and the learning is
consolidated in a short debrief. Concepts are discovered through the activity rather than delivered before it. Students
experience a bottleneck, a culture clash, or a failed handoff first, and name the principle afterward.
Functional Coverage
The curriculum is mapped against the full set of business functional areas so no core discipline is missed. Major functions
sources.keywords: organizational-design-high-school.pdf · page 1

sources.title: organizational-design-high-school.pdf · page 1
sources.content:
each receive dedicated weeks; secondary functions (supply chain, IT/data, PR and crisis communications) are addressed
through scenario cards embedded in later units and the capstone crisis round, giving honest coverage without inflating the
calendar. Content cross-over allows for the reinforcement of previously learned objectives.
Relationship to the Leadership Mindset Course
Some students take the parallel Leadership Mindset course, which builds an individual operating system (lead yourself, then
lead others). This course is the collective counterpart: what happens when individually-led people must build a structure,
culture, and management system together. Frameworks shared between the two — Tuckman's stages, SBI feedback, Circle
of Control, PDCA — function here as reinforcement in a new context. The course stands fully on its own.
ASSESSMENT

Assessment is performance-based. Students are evaluated on the artifacts they produce for their company (org chart, SOPs,
budget, service policy, contract, risk audit) and on the capstone, where teams present their complete organization to an
authentic audience and respond to a surprise crisis scenario in real time.
Guest Speakers
Guest speakers representing various organizational types may share their lessons learned, as scheduled.
Use of AI
Use of ChatGPT, Claude Co-work, and Grok Imagine may be used to complete course objectives.

Unit Weeks Focus

Marketing, Sales &
Customers 18–22 Research, messaging, selling, service recovery

the activity-based model, most objectives sit at the Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, and Create levels — students demonstrate
understanding by doing, deciding, and building rather than by recalling.

sources.content:
Is River Tech right for your child?
We want your child to enjoy what makes River Tech distinctive. Just as a culinary school suits someone interested in cooking, River Tech suits students interested in technology, performing arts, or both. If neither appeals to your child, another school may be a better fit.
About your family
Tell us who you are and how we can reach you.
Your first name*
Your last name*
Email*
Phone*
City*
Were you introduced to River Tech by one of our families?
About your children
Add each child you hope to enroll. For more than four children, include the others in the final notes box.
Program and timing
Your answers help us identify openings that could work for your family.
Which program are you hoping for?*
Full-Time — four or five days a week, the complete River Tech experience.
À La Carte — one to four days a week, alongside your homeschool.
Either one — we are open to both programs; we simply hope to join.
Which days interest you?
Monday — Performing Arts
Tuesday — Science & Social Studies
Thursday — Life Skills
Friday — Technology
When would you hope to start?*
January 2027 — we would happily take a mid-year seat.
September 2027 — we are planning for next fall.
Whenever a seat opens — we are flexible.
If offered a place, how soon could your child start?*If places open at different times, could your children start separately?
Our culture
River Tech has a distinct culture, and it matters more than anything else on this form. Please take a few minutes to read Our Culture — it is a plain and honest description of who we are.
We have read Our Culture, and it describes a school we want for our family.*
Our full-time school day begins with worship, prayer, and a short devotional, and everything we teach — in every program, on every day — reflects a Christian worldview. Our family is comfortable with this, and we support it.*
Tuition, stated plainly
Full-time tuition for 2026–27 is $7,800 for five days or $6,716 for four when paid quarterly. A $250 household enrollment fee for full-time school is due only after a seat is offered and accepted. See the tuition page for all plans, À La Carte fees, and payment options. Eligible Idaho families may apply for the Parental Choice Tax Credit; an award is not automatic.
If a seat is offered, which payment plan would your family use?*
Quarterly · Our standard plan (recommended).
Annually — one payment at the start of the year.Monthly · 12 payments, July through June.
Would your child’s enrollment depend on receiving a scholarship from River Tech?*
No — we can carry tuition without a scholarship.
Yes — we would need a scholarship to enroll.
We have reviewed the tuition above, and our family can meet the payments on time for the full school year.*
Anything else?
This one is entirely optional.
Joining is free and does not commit you to enroll or guarantee a place. We contact wait-pool families first; public enrollment happens only if places remain. If your plans change, email learn@rivertech.me.

Review the trip details & school schedule
Where & when
Location: River City Lanes Bowling / Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026 / Bowling time: 10:00–11:30 AM / Cost: $12 per person, including bowling, shoe rental, and taxes.
Full-time students
Full-time students joining the field trip should be dropped off at school between 8:10–8:30 AM and picked up at 2:30 PM, as usual. Transportation will be provided by our school bus, although a few Junior High and High School students may ride with Jordan, Caitlin, Luke, or Mary.
Part-time students
Meet us at River City Lanes at 9:45 AM and pick up by 11:30 AM. You are welcome to join us for park play after; see the school schedule below.
Part-time students must have a supervising adult. For this specific field trip, part-time students ages 13 and older may be dropped off with a River Tech teacher, without their own supervising adult. For students ages 12 and younger, text Mary to request permission to drop off your child without a supervising adult, if needed and if your child is independent enough.
Activities & cost
Bowling: $12 per participant, including shoe rental and taxes. Payment is collected through the sign-up form. River City Lanes will have a cosmic light show and song requests!
Arcade games: Optional! Students may bring extra cash to play arcade games. Not included in the bowling fee.
Food & snacks: The full River City Lanes menu will be available for purchase. Students may also bring their own cold lunch, snacks, or small treats to share with classmates and friends.
Costumes: Students are welcome to dress up! Please avoid costumes that may frighten younger children. No face-covering masks, weapons, blood, or gore.
Part-time student chaperones: Adults who bowl must register and pay $12, including those who are also supervising students. Adults who attend only to supervise and will not bowl do not need to register or pay.
School schedule for November 4
There will be no school that day for students who are not participating in the field trip.
For participating full-time students, we will begin with our usual morning assembly and have Math and English classes before and after the field trip. Weather permitting, we also plan to visit the Real Life outdoor and indoor playgrounds from 11:45 AM–12:45 PM before returning to school. Part-time students are welcome to join us at the playgrounds as well if they would like, with their supervising adult!
Please note that the schedule and playground destination are subject to change.
If you need to drop off your full-time student late or pick them up early, please text their Math or English teacher directly to coordinate. If you are unsure whom to contact, text Mary.
Sign-up & payment
Deadline: Sunday, November 1, at midnight (Pacific time).
Complete the form and payment to reserve your student's spot. If you miss the deadline, text Mary to check whether space is still available. Spots cannot be guaranteed after Sunday. Late places require Mary's approval and payment to Mary in cash.

I also authorize emergency medical care for my child and accept responsibility for related medical expenses.

River Tech is built for artistic and tech-savvy kids who love music and technology. Alongside core subjects like math, language arts, social science, and science, students learn technology and performing arts every day. Class sizes are around 15 students, roughly half of most public schools. Our teachers spend real time with each child, and students move at their own pace through a competency-based model grounded in Christian values.

TECHNOLOGY
River Tech is a School of Technology. Students learn coding, digital arts, 3D modeling, robotics, filmmaking, digital design, Legos, and engineering. Hands-on every day: learning by doing, building projects, and playing.

PERFORMING ARTS
River Tech is a School of Performing Arts with a program that includes recording, production, and live performance. Each student learns drums, bass, ukulele, guitar, keyboard, band, vocals, choir, dance, acting, and musical theater.
