What is the culture like at River Tech?
River Tech is a Christian school built on biblical principles. Each day begins with a worship song, prayer, and a short devotional, and faith runs through the day rather than being set aside during classes. We raise kids to love God, honor their families, contribute to their community, take responsibility for themselves, work hard, and build things worth building. We don’t teach gender ideology, critical race theory, victim mentality, or cancel culture. Children attending River Tech Days get to take part in that life alongside our full-time students.

What should my child bring?
Standard school supplies such as a notepad, pencils, eraser, and pencil sharpener, and, importantly, a device. Students who choose coding or 3D modeling must bring their own laptop. Starting in 2nd grade, students should bring a tablet for class use. Around age 10, students should transition to a laptop.

💻 MacBook (2020 or newer)
💻 Windows laptop: Intel Core i5 (8th gen) or AMD Ryzen 5 3500U, 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD, NVIDIA GTX 1050 or AMD RX 560, Windows 10 (64-bit)
📱 iPad (2020 or newer)
📱 Android tablet: Qualcomm Snapdragon 670, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, Android 9.0 or newer

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · SCHOOL CULTURE
sources.content:
Handbook section: SCHOOL CULTURE. Document dated October 30, 2026.
Idaho Roots
River Tech reflects the character of our region. Idaho runs on faith, family, hard work, and time spent outdoors, and so do we. Kids grow best when school and home share the same direction, and we want parents to know ours before they enroll.
A Christian School
Our staff are Christians, and the shape of the school day reflects that. We open each morning with worship, prayer, and a short devotional. Faith runs through the day rather than being set aside during classes.
We welcome families from many different churches, and we don't promote one denomination over another. C.S. Lewis had a phrase for this: “mere Christianity,” a shared foundation that honors the core of the faith while leaving the details to churches and parents.
A Small School, on Purpose
Our classes are small, about fifteen students, because that's the size where a school can actually know a child. Every teacher knows every student by name, knows what they're working on, and notices when something is off. We lean on parents, too, for volunteer days, guest teaching, field-trip help, and honest feedback about what's working and what isn't. River Tech is a community, and your family is part of it.
What We Stand For, and What We Don't
We stand for God, family, church, community, personal responsibility, patriotism, merit, grit, and entrepreneurship.
We don't teach gender ideology, critical race theory, victim mentality, or cancel culture. We are committed instead to a stable, time-tested framework that fosters character, strength, clarity, and wisdom.
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · SCHOOL CULTURE

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · SCHOOL CULTURE
sources.content:
Students are addressed as boys and girls. Our teachers prepare students for adult life, including courtship, marriage, and parenting. But our students do not engage in idle talk about crushes, romantic relationships, or LGBTQ.
Grit
Kids need challenge to become capable adults. A child should never experience abuse, harm, or bullying, but they should absolutely experience discomfort, frustration, and the feeling of something genuinely hard, in order to become resilient under pressure.
We spend about twenty minutes each day on drill and calisthenics. Drill teaches focus, posture, and the discipline of moving as a group. Calisthenics builds real physical readiness. Once a week we head to the park, and every three weeks or so we take a field trip, often something physical like wall climbing, trampoline jumping, or roller skating. We celebrate the wins, too, from birthdays and finished projects to end-of-term parties and the kind of everyday moments that make kids feel at home.
We're a technology school, but we believe real-life experiences are foundational for healthy growth. That's why we balance tech classes with performing arts, liberal arts, and life skills, and that's why we protect the things technology can't replace: family time, real friendships, time in nature, creative work, and a growing faith.
How We Teach Hard Things
Our classrooms take on the great stories, histories, and ideas of the world, including the difficult ones. War, mythology, and competing worldviews are central to understanding the human story, and we don't flinch from them. We teach them with Christian commentary and a conservative frame, so that students come away with moral clarity rather than moral confusion.
Culture Expressed Through Conduct
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · SCHOOL CULTURE

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · SCHOOL CULTURE
sources.content:
At River Tech, our values are not abstract ideals — they are lived daily through conduct.
The RIVER framework is the practical expression of our culture. These values are also known as the school values.
Responsibility — Personal Responsibility & Grit
Culture: hard work, perseverance, stewardship
Expression: prompt obedience, ownership, follow-through
Integrity — Christian Moral Foundation
Culture: biblical truth, honesty, character
Expression: truthfulness, honesty in work, confession of mistakes
Voice — Ordered, Respectful Community
Culture: respect, honor, community stability
Expression: controlled speech, no vulgarity, respectful tone
Excellence — Merit, Discipline, Craftsmanship
Culture: merit, entrepreneurship, growth mentality
Expression: quality work, presentation, seriousness of effort
Respect — Honor, Authority, Community Order
Culture: family, authority, social order
Expression: obedience, no bullying, honoring people and property

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
Handbook section: STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT. Document dated October 30, 2026.
1. Overview
The purpose of the River Tech Student Code of Conduct is to encourage students to follow Christian standards of behavior by clearly indicating acceptable behavior.
River Tech exists to cultivate bright minds and disciplined character. Discipline is not primarily about punishment. It is about formation.
“For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth.” — Proverbs 3:12
Correction is an act of care. Standards are an act of love. When these standards are violated, behavior will be corrected calmly and consistently.
The RIVER Values
At River Tech, student conduct is guided by the RIVER values:
* Responsibility — We do what is expected promptly, carefully, and without being chased.
* Integrity — We tell the truth, take ownership of our actions, and do what is right even when no one is watching.
* Voice — We use words, tone, and timing that are respectful, clean, and fitting for the moment.
* Excellence — We complete our work and carry ourselves with professionalism, care, and purpose.
* Respect — We honor people, property, time, and authority through our conduct and attitude.
River Tech students move like the river — steady, directed, and powerful.
The Student Pledge
“Don’t let anyone look down on you because you are young, but set an example for the believers in speech, in life, in love, in faith, and in purity.” 1 Timothy 4:12
1. I will submit to the civil authority of our country and obey its laws. I understand this will prohibit such things as the use of tobacco of any kind, alcohol, marijuana, vaping, the illegal use of drugs of any kind as defined by federal law, gambling and shoplifting. (I Timothy 2:1-2, I Peter 2:13-14)
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
2. I will willingly submit to those in authority over me. (I Thessalonians 5:12, I Peter 5:5)
* Example: a teacher asks you to sit down after you’ve stood up and walked about the room.
* Don’t: argue with the teacher or make a scene.
* Do: sit back down promptly and raise your hand if you need permission to get up.
3. I will respect and honor other individuals. (1 Peter 2:17; Philippians 2:3; and Galatians 5:14)
* This includes: interrupting someone while they are speaking, name calling, fighting, belittling, etc.
4. I will respect the property of others. (Exodus 10:15, Leviticus 19:11, I Thessalonians 4:6)
* This includes: not touching others property without permission, damaging, or stealing, this goes for school property as well. Accidentally causing damage to property is still a concern; report any accidental damage immediately to a staff member.
5. I will conduct myself with honor and integrity in both spoken and written Word. (Colossians 3:9-10, 4:6, Titus 2:6-8)
* This includes: no filthy, crude, vulgar or inappropriate language or lying.
6. I will use wholesome speech that respects the name of God, Christianity, and His Church. (Exodus 20:7; Ephesians 4:29; and Hebrews 10:29)
* Though you may have disagreements, maintain language that emphasizes respect and consideration for others beliefs.
7. I will be modest in my dress and appearance. I have read and understand the applicable sections of the Student Handbook related to dress and appearance. (I Thessalonians 4:3-7, I Timothy 2:9-10, I Peter 3:3-5)
8. I will use technology in an appropriate and responsible manner. (Psalm 105:21, Luke 16:1-2, James 3:13-3)
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
* This includes: only using school approved applications during school hours. School-approved applications are listed on the school’s website or can be provided by your teacher.
9. I will inform an administrator or teacher if I learn about anyone threatening to harm themselves or others. (Ecclesiastes 8:11, John 13:34, I Thessalonians 4:9)
* Report any threats of harm, whether to oneself or others, including verbal threats or actions that suggest potential harm.
2. Standards of Conduct
Responsibility
Responsibility reflects maturity, stewardship, and prompt obedience.
“Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.” — 1 Corinthians 4:2
Students are expected to demonstrate:
1. Prompt obedience to instruction
2. Composure in transitions
3. Situational awareness
4. Care for property and shared spaces
5. Accountability in daily responsibilities
Examples include:
* Walking indoors
* Immediate response to school signals
* Orderly and efficient lineup formation
* Leaving spaces better than they were found
* Completing expected tasks without repeated prompting
* Completing and turning in assigned work
Repeated irresponsibility becomes a discipline concern.
“He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul.” — Proverbs 15:32
Integrity
Integrity reflects truthfulness, honesty, and personal ownership.
“Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.” — 2 Corinthians 8:21
Students are expected to:
* Tell the truth
* Take responsibility for their actions
* Complete work honestly
* Admit mistakes without deception
* Do what is right even when unobserved
Examples of integrity violations may include:
* Lying
* Cheating
* Hiding wrongdoing
* Blaming others falsely
* Misrepresenting work or conduct
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
* Theft — taking something that does not belong to you
Serious dishonesty may result in immediate administrative involvement.
“He that walketh uprightly walketh surely.” — Proverbs 10:9
Voice
Voice reflects speech, tone, timing, and verbal self-control.
“Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying.” — Ephesians 4:29
Students must:
* Avoid profanity and crude language
* Avoid mocking, degrading, or sarcastically disruptive speech
* Speak respectfully to peers, staff, and guests
* Use an appropriate tone when asking questions or responding to correction
* Contribute to an orderly verbal environment
Directed profanity, verbal harassment, or threatening speech are considered major violations. See section 6, Speech and Language.
“A soft answer turneth away wrath.” — Proverbs 15:1
Excellence
Excellence reflects professionalism, discipline, quality, and presentation.
“Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.” — Ecclesiastes 9:10
Students are expected to:
* Complete work with care and purpose
* Follow dress and appearance standards
* Carry themselves in a neat, prepared, and disciplined way
* Use devices properly as tools for learning
* Approach school responsibilities with seriousness
This includes:
* Following posted dress expectations
* Maintaining a neat, distraction-free appearance
* Using devices only when permitted and for assigned purposes
* Remaining on task
* Avoiding careless or disorderly habits in work and conduct
Repeated disregard for standards of presentation, work quality, or device use may become a discipline concern.
“Let all things be done decently and in order.” — 1 Corinthians 14:40
Respect
Respect reflects honor shown toward others, authority, property, and the learning environment.
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” — Romans 12:10
Students are expected to:
* Treat others with dignity
* Respond appropriately to authority
* Keep hands to themselves
* Avoid bullying, intimidation, or harassment
* Handle property and shared spaces properly, and never damage property on purpose
* Be where they are scheduled to be, and not leave a class or area without permission
* Contribute to an orderly and safe school culture
Aggressive, threatening, or openly defiant behavior will result in immediate administrative involvement.
“Blessed are the peacemakers.” — Matthew 5:9
3. Discipline Policy
Purpose & Principle
Discipline is both good and necessary. (Proverbs 13:24, Proverbs 29:15, Proverbs 19:17)
River Tech uses a clear three-tier response model: Tier 1: teacher correction; Tier 2: teacher-to-parent contact for repeated minor behavior; Tier 3: administrative involvement when behavior continues after parent contact or is major from the outset. Minor and major violations remain the two classifications of conduct. Correction is calm, brief, and consistent.
“Let all things be done decently and in order.” — 1 Corinthians 14:40
Minor Violations (Teacher Managed)
Minor violations are isolated departures from expected standards.
Examples may include:
* Running indoors
* Talking during instruction
* Minor dress corrections
* First-time device misuse
* Mild disrespect
* Avoidable or careless language
* Careless messes or disorder
* Incomplete assigned work
* Delayed compliance that ends when corrected
Teacher response may include:
* Immediate correction
* If applicable, reset (redo properly)
* Brief restorative action
* Documentation if behavior becomes repetitive
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
* Direct teacher-to-parent contact when the same minor behavior continues after correction.
* Administrative referral if the behavior continues after parent contact or crosses into major conduct.
“A soft answer turneth away wrath.” — Proverbs 15:1
Administrative escalation occurs when conduct is a major violation, when a student refuses correction in a way that constitutes blatant defiance, or when a repeated minor behavior continues after teacher correction and parent contact.
Teacher-to-Parent Contact for Repeated Minor Violations
When an isolated minor violation is corrected but the same behavior recurs or the correction does not produce follow-through, the teacher will contact the student’s parent or guardian directly. Contact may occur by phone, text, email, or a brief conversation at pickup.
Teacher-to-parent contact is the final teacher-managed step before administrative escalation for an ordinary pattern of minor behavior. If the behavior continues after parent contact, the matter may be referred to administration as an established pattern.
This intermediate step does not apply when conduct is already a major violation. Blatant defiance, aggression, harassment, threats, serious dishonesty, safety concerns, or other major behavior may be referred to administration immediately.
Major Violations (Administrative)
Major violations involve:
* Blatant defiance
* Physical aggression
* Harassment or bullying
* Directed profanity
* Threats
* Serious device misuse
* Academic dishonesty
* Theft or intentional damage to property
* Leaving class or campus without permission
* Serious disrespect toward authority
* An established pattern of repeated minor violations that continues after teacher correction and teacher-to-parent contact, when applicable
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
Administrative responses may include:
* Administrative follow-up with parents and staff
* Detention
* Restitution
* Restorative service, for example cleaning the commons area
* Loss of privileges
* Behavior contract
* Suspension
* Expulsion, when necessary
“He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.” — Proverbs 28:13
Pattern & Trajectory
A single mistake does not define a student.
“Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” — Galatians 6:7
When a pattern begins to develop, the teacher documents the concern and contacts the parent or guardian directly. If the behavior continues after that contact, administrative intervention may occur. Discipline addresses direction, not isolated imperfection.
Restoration
When behavior damages order, relationship, trust, property, or community culture, students may be required to:
* Redo the behavior properly
* Offer an apology
* Repair damage
* Make restitution
* Participate in restorative action or service
“First be reconciled to thy brother.” — Matthew 5:24
Restoration is the goal.
Transitions, Readiness, and School Order
Prompt obedience and orderly movement are expected throughout the school day.
“Obey them that have the rule over you.” — Hebrews 13:17
When signals or instructions are given, students are expected to respond immediately, appropriately, and without unnecessary delay. This includes:
* Stopping when directed
* Moving promptly and with control
* Forming quietly and efficiently
* Being prepared for transitions and instruction
Failure to meet transition standards may result in retraining, corrective resets, or further discipline when needed.
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
Repeated classroom-order or transition concerns follow the same progression used for other minor violations: teacher correction and reset, teacher-to-parent contact if the correction does not hold, and administrative involvement if the behavior continues.
Gold & Privileges
Gold reflects positive contribution and faithful stewardship.
“Well done, thou good and faithful servant.” — Matthew 25:21
Discipline and Gold operate separately. Gold is earned through positive contribution; it is not deducted as a disciplinary penalty. See School Currency.
Eligibility for certain privileges may require:
* No major violations
* Demonstrated responsibility
* Positive behavioral trajectory
4. Progressive Intervention & Enrollment Determination
River Tech is committed to restoration before removal.
“Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness.” — Galatians 6:1
Discipline is designed to correct direction and preserve community culture. When patterns of misconduct emerge, the following process will be used.
Phase 1: Correction & Awareness
At this stage:
* Minor violations are corrected by staff
* Patterns are documented
* The teacher contacts the parent or guardian when an initial correction does not produce lasting follow-through.
* The teacher, parent, and student work toward early realignment.
* Administration may be consulted for guidance without formally taking over the matter.
* Private conversations may be held
Goal: realignment and growth.
Phase 2: Formal Concern & Intervention
This phase is initiated when:
* Repeated minor violations establish a pattern
* Disrespect becomes habitual
* Authority is persistently resisted
* Conduct undermines school culture
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
* Growth is not occurring through ordinary correction and teacher-to-parent contact
At this stage:
* A meeting is scheduled with parents
* A written behavior contract may be issued
* Clear expectations and measurable standards are outlined
* A review window, typically 30–45 days, is established
The purpose is restoration and demonstrated growth.
Phase 3: Enrollment Determination
If, after formal intervention:
* The pattern continues
* Correction is persistently resisted
* The student undermines authority or community culture
* Growth is not demonstrated within the review period
Leadership may determine that River Tech is not the appropriate environment for the student at this time. This determination is not made lightly.
“A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.” — Galatians 5:9
River Tech must protect the integrity of its academic and relational culture for the benefit of the entire student body.
Separation decisions may include:
* Withdrawal recommendation
* Non-renewal of enrollment
* Expulsion in severe cases
Immediate Removal
Certain behaviors may result in immediate suspension or expulsion without progressive phases, including:
* Physical violence
* Threats of harm
* Serious harassment
* Severe academic dishonesty
* Weapons on campus
* Drugs, tobacco, or alcohol
* Actions that compromise safety
Important Clarification
Removal is not based solely on the number of infractions. It is based on:
* Trajectory
* Responsiveness to correction
* Influence on community culture
* Willingness to align with River Tech standards
Our goal is restoration. However, consistent rejection of correction may indicate that River Tech is not the right fit.
5. Harassment/Bullying/Threats
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
An important part of River Tech’s educational curriculum is developing each child’s social capital through: team building, emotional and social competence, cultivation of empathy, and anti-bullying workshops. We aim to teach our students to get along with others who may differ from them. We also want to cultivate a culture of volunteerism, charity, and missions.
Bullying, threats, and harassment, whether sexual, ethnic, racial, age, religious, or handicap-related, will not be tolerated at River Tech. Students subjected to or observing bullying need to report incidents to a teacher immediately. Written and/or verbal threats of bodily harm to students or staff will be taken very seriously. Any student making a threat regardless of intent, whether jokingly or not, may be subject to suspension or expulsion.
Harassment, bullying, and threats are major violations and involve administration immediately.
6. Speech and Language
Speech is classified in three levels, and each level is handled under the three-tier response model in section 3.
Level 1 — Avoidable Language
Words or phrases that are unnecessary, mildly inappropriate, or commonly discouraged in a respectful environment, for example “dang it” or “that’s dumb.”
* Handled as a minor violation: immediate verbal correction by the teacher.
Level 2 — Targeted Language
Language directed at others in a hurtful or disrespectful manner, for example “you’re stupid” or “shut up.”
* Handled as a minor violation on first occurrence: stronger verbal correction, a clear warning about escalation, and documentation.
* If the behavior recurs, the teacher contacts the parent or guardian directly.
* Continued targeted language after parent contact moves to administrative response.
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
* Language that becomes harassment, threatening speech, or another major violation involves administration immediately.
Level 3 — Profanity and Vulgarity
Any use of explicit, vulgar, or profane language, whether directed at others or spoken in frustration.
* Handled as a major violation: administrative involvement, parent contact, and restorative action or service.
* Directed profanity, verbal harassment, and threatening speech are always major violations.
7. Devices
Devices are tools for learning. They must be used in appropriate manners and at appropriate times. See Portable Electronic Devices for what students may bring.
* First or isolated misuse is a minor violation: teacher correction, and the device is confiscated until the end of the day.
* Repeated misuse is documented by the teacher and followed by direct parent or guardian contact. A parent may be required to retrieve the device.
* Continued misuse after parent contact becomes a major violation and moves to administrative response. Device privileges may be suspended for a defined period.
* Serious device misuse is a major violation from the first instance. This includes accessing prohibited content, circumventing the school safety network, installing unapproved non-educational applications, and using a device to harass, record, or deceive.
* Cellular devices remain in backpacks throughout the day. A phone used during the day is confiscated until the end of the day.
8. Plagiarism
Plagiarism is defined as the act of presenting other people’s ideas and writings as one’s own and/or not giving credit to the original source(s). This action is not allowed at River Tech.
AI tools such as ChatGPT are not permitted for use on school assignments unless a teacher says otherwise.
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
Academic dishonesty is a major violation. Severe academic dishonesty may result in immediate removal.
9. Weapons Policy
Students who bring knives, guns or objects constructed as weapons onto school property or to school-sponsored activities will be subject to suspension or expulsion per Idaho Code 33-205 and 18-3302D. For special occasions we may allow the exception of toys that are clearly not close to misrepresenting real weapons. IE. Nerf, Foam, etc.
10. Drug, Tobacco, and Alcohol Policy
In compliance with the Drug Free School and Communities Act Amendments of 1989 (PL100-690) River Tech recognizes its responsibility to maintain a school environment free of drugs, tobacco, and alcohol. Violation of this policy may result in suspension or expulsion, and notification of parents/guardians.
11. Dress Code
Purpose & Principle
River Tech’s daily wear standard supports learning, safety, focus, modesty, and professionalism while promoting school identity and parity among students. Our emphasis is on character over appearance (1 Peter 3:3–4). Uniforms are optional; daily wear is flexible within these standards.
Helpful test: Would you feel confident sending your student to a job interview in this outfit?
Detailed Guide
Tops
* Collared polos, henleys, blouses, button-downs, knit tops, t-shirts, crewneck/V-neck sweaters, and cardigans.
* Sleeveless OK with straps ≥ 2.5 inches; arm openings fitted.
* Opaque fabrics appropriate for school.
* Necklines remain professional; keep cleavage covered.
Bottoms
* Chinos/khakis, trousers, joggers(PE only), and neat denim.
* Shorts/skirts/skorts/dresses: fingertip length or longer.
* Distressing refined: any hole ≤ half-dollar and not exposing skin above fingertip length.
Coverage & Fit
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
* Midriff and seat remain covered during normal activity.
* Garments fit securely at the waist for a polished, professional look.
* Garments can be loose overall but not overly baggy.
* Undergarments remain fully covered.
Footwear
* Daily wear: clean, secure shoes suited to indoor/outdoor movement.
* Safety-dependent activities (labs, shop, certain field trips): closed-toe required.
* P.E.: running shoes and athletic socks.
Layers & Outerwear
* In-class: sweaters, cardigans, light jackets, vests, school-spirit outerwear.
* Arrival/dismissal/outdoors: sunglasses, bandanas, scarves, heavy coats; store during class unless needed for health.
Accessories & Jewelry
* Subtle, safe, distraction-free.
* Piercing jewelry worn in ears only (modest studs/hoops).
* No spikes, sharp hardware, or unsafe accessories.
* Belts, watches, simple bracelets/necklaces welcome when subtle/safe.
Hair & Grooming
* Clean, neat, professional.
* No carved names/symbols/numbers.
* One natural hair color; natural-colored highlights/lowlights allowed.
* Facial hair neatly trimmed.
Makeup & Nails
* Moderate and well-kept; naturally-colored; suited to a professional/educational setting.
Graphics, Messages, and Symbols
* Allowed when school-appropriate and aligned with River Tech values.
* Not allowed: violence, drugs/alcohol/tobacco, profanity, sexual content, or demeaning themes.
P.E. & Active Wear
* Required: running shoes; athletic shorts/sweats/joggers; athletic top.
* Length and coverage standards apply. Tie back long hair for safety.
Definition — Normal Activity: walking, sitting, standing, bending, and/or stretching.
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT
sources.content:
Below is a visual reference of what to wear/not wear. Pictures that are sloppy/inappropriate will showcase many examples of dress code violations, though the overall look is wrong, pay attention to why each detail was added.
Dress Code Enforcement
* An isolated dress correction is a minor violation, handled by the teacher with a quiet correction and, where possible, an on-the-spot fix.
* If the same concern recurs after correction, the teacher contacts the parent or guardian directly and documents the contact.
* If the concern continues after parent contact, it becomes an established pattern and moves to administrative response.
* Deliberate defiance or another major violation may be referred to administration immediately.
12. Final Standard
River Tech students are expected to pursue:
* Self-control
* Prompt obedience
* Truthfulness
* Respectful speech
* Professional conduct
* Composure
* Integrity
“Add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge… and to knowledge temperance.” — 2 Peter 1:5–6
Students who consistently reject these standards may not be a fit for River Tech’s academic and spiritual culture.
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · PARENT/STUDENT GRIEVANCES
sources.content:
Handbook section: PARENT/STUDENT GRIEVANCES. Document dated October 30, 2026.
Purpose & Principle
Resolve concerns promptly, fairly, and biblically—protecting relationships, supporting learning, and strengthening our school community.
Biblical Foundation
* Matthew 18:15–17 – Go first to the person privately; then include one or two others; then bring it to leadership if still unresolved.
* Galatians 6:1 – Restore gently.
* Ephesians 4:15 – Speak the truth in love.
* James 1:19–20 – Quick to listen, slow to speak, slow to anger.
* Proverbs 15:1 – A gentle answer turns away wrath.
Guiding Principles
1. Start small & close (speak directly to the person first when safe/appropriate).
2. Seek understanding (listen first; clarify facts).
3. Be timely (address concerns promptly).
4. Respect privacy (avoid gossip; protect dignity).
5. Pursue resolution (agree on clear next steps).
6. No retaliation (good-faith concerns are protected).
Scheduling note: When a meeting is needed in pathways B–D, the parent or student should email the teacher to request and schedule the meeting. If the concern reaches the Principal step, email the Principal and cc the teacher.
(For A. Student↔Student, students go in person to the teacher—no email needed.)
Processes by Situation
A. Student Concern with Another Student
1. Student → Student (private conversation) – Student shares the concern respectfully and proposes a repair (ideally within 2 school days).
2. Student → Teacher (awareness + mediation) – If unresolved, the student goes in person to the shared teacher to make them aware and request mediation. The teacher facilitates a restorative mediation and records the outcome.
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · PARENT/STUDENT GRIEVANCES

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · PARENT/STUDENT GRIEVANCES
sources.content:
3. Teacher-coordinated parent meeting – If mediation fails, the teacher reaches out to both sets of parents to schedule a joint meeting with the teacher mediating.
4. Principal involvement (final step) – If still unresolved, escalate to the Principal for next steps/restorative plan. The Principal’s decision is final.
B. Parent Concern about a Student Situation
1. Parent → Shared Teacher – Parent emails the teacher (homeroom or relevant class) to schedule a meeting; teacher facilitates resolution.
2. Parent + Principal (final step) – If unresolved, parent emails the Principal (cc teacher) to schedule a meeting. The Principal’s decision is final.
C. Student Concern with a Teacher
1. Student → Teacher – Student shares concern privately; if a meeting is needed, the student emails the teacher to schedule.
2. Student + Principal (final step) – If unresolved, student emails the Principal (cc teacher) to schedule. The Principal’s decision is final.
D. Parent Concern with a Teacher
1. Parent → Teacher – Parent emails the teacher to request and schedule a meeting.
2. Parent + Principal (final step) – If unresolved, parent emails the Principal (cc teacher) to schedule. The Principal’s decision is final.
Communication Standards (All Steps)
* Use specific facts/examples; avoid assumptions and labels.
* Assume good intent; ask clarifying questions.
* Confidentiality: share details only with those directly involved in resolution.
* Documentation: staff note the concern, date, participants, and agreed next steps.
* Email is the default channel for scheduling meetings (teacher first; Principal when escalated).
Safety & Mandatory Exceptions
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · PARENT/STUDENT GRIEVANCES

sources.title: River Tech Handbook · PARENT/STUDENT GRIEVANCES
sources.content:
Skip directly to the Principal (and authorities as required) for immediate risk, harassment, discrimination, self-harm, abuse, or other legally reportable concerns. River Tech complies with all mandatory reporting laws.
Principal email: learn@rivertech.me
Non-Retaliation
No student, parent, or staff member will be penalized for raising a good-faith concern. Retaliation results in disciplinary action.
Final Decision
The Principal is the final authority for grievance decisions at River Tech.
Outcomes & Restoration
Outcomes may include clarifications, apologies, seating/class adjustments, restorative conferences, behavior contracts, consequences per the handbook, and follow-up check-ins. Aim for restored relationships and a healthy learning environment.
Quick Flow
* Student vs. Student: Student → Student → Teacher (in-person awareness + mediation) → Teacher sets joint parent meeting → Principal (final)
* Parent about Student Issue: Parent → Email Shared Teacher → Email Principal (cc teacher) — final
* Student vs. Teacher: Student → Email Teacher → Email Principal (cc teacher) — final
* Parent vs. Teacher: Parent → Email Teacher → Email Principal (cc teacher) — final
* Emergency/Safety: Contact Principal immediately (and authorities if required)
sources.keywords: River Tech Handbook · PARENT/STUDENT GRIEVANCES

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · setup
sources.content:
1 · Setting up
You need an email address you can open today. That's all.
New to River Tech? Apply first at
rivertech.me/enrollment. Applying does not
make an account. Once you've applied, come back here and make one.
The school may have set you up already. If you got an email from River Tech
asking you to set a password, use that link instead, then skip to
Link your child.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · setup

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · create
sources.content:
Create your account
Go to rivertech.me.
Press Create a Parent Account (under the Login button).
Fill in the form and press Register.
Use your own name, not your child's.
Your password needs at least 8 characters.
There's no box for your child here. You link them in step 3.
Each email address can only have one account, so don't use the same
address you plan to give your child.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · create

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · confirm
sources.content:
Confirm your email
Open the email from River Tech.
Click the link in it.
You'll see "✅ Email Confirmed!" and then land back in the portal,
signed in.
No email after a few minutes? Check your spam folder. Still nothing, or
the link says it has expired? Don't register again (it won't let you). Email
learn@rivertech.me and the office will
open the account for you.
Next time, just sign in at rivertech.me with
your email and password. Bookmark that address. It's the only one you need.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · confirm

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · link
sources.content:
Link your child
When you first sign in, your home screen looks like this. That's expected:
Press ➕ Link a Child. There are two ways to do it.
⚡ With a link code (fastest)
Ask the office for your child's link code. It looks like
ABCD2345.
Press "Have a link code from the school?" at the bottom.
Type the code and press Link with code.
Your child appears right away.
✉️ Without a code
Type your child's full name, spelled the way the school has it.
Add their grade if you like.
Press Send Request.
Someone at the school checks it and emails you when it's done.
More than one child? Do this once for each child, using
➕ Link Another Child. Each child has their own code.
The name box won't suggest names as you type. That's on purpose, to keep
students' names private.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · link

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · openchild
sources.content:
Give your child their own sign-in (optional)
If your child's card says they have no sign-in yet, the school has their
record but they can't sign in themselves. To fix that:
On your home screen, press ✉️ Open (your child's name)'s account on their card.
Type an email address your child can open. It can't be your own.
Tick the box to confirm it's right, and press Send the link.
Your child gets an email to set their own password. Everything the school
already has for them (classes, grades, skills) is waiting when they sign in.
Younger children without an email can still play the learning games with a
4-character Games PIN from their teacher.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · openchild

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · around
sources.content:
Finding your way around
After you sign in you land on 🏠 Home. Most things live one click away, under
📊 Portal. The bar across the top always takes you between them:
| Button | What's there
| 🏠 Home | Your children, a school calendar, and days of school left.
| 📊 Portal | Your children's progress and every quick action (absence, late or early, transcript).
| 📚 Children's Classes | Each class your children take, with assignments, grades and teacher notes.
| 💬 Messages | Write to your children's teachers and the office.
| 👤 Profile | Your password, email, which emails you get, and how the site looks.
The 🔔 bell next to the bar tells you about new assignments, graded work and
new messages.
On 📊 Portal, each child shows a badge like
0/3. That's their behavior strikes: green is
none, amber is one or two, red is three. Strikes clear on their own over time, and
you're always emailed when one is given.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · around

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · absence
sources.content:
Reporting an absence
No phone call needed. On 📊 Portal, press 📅 Report an Absence:
Pick your child.
Pick the first and last day they'll be away. One day? Pick the same day
twice. Weekends in between are skipped for you.
Add a reason if you like (for example "unwell").
Press Tell the school.
The school is told straight away, and you'll see how many staff were notified.
Already reported at the top of the window shows absences already on file,
so you won't send the same one twice.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · absence

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · lateearly
sources.content:
Late arrival or early pickup
For a dentist visit in the morning or a pickup before the end of the day. On
📊 Portal, press ⏰ Late Arrival / Early Pickup:
Pick your child.
Choose Arriving late or Picking up early.
Pick the day (today or later) and the time.
Add a reason if you like, and press Tell the school.
Your child's teachers and the office are told straight away. Plans changed? Press
Withdraw next to it under Already reported.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · lateearly

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · messages
sources.content:
Messaging a teacher
Press 💬 Messages in the top bar.
Under To:, pick the teacher (or the office).
Type your message and press ✉️ Send Message.
Replies show under 📬 Recent Messages, and the 🔔 bell lights up when one
arrives. The list shows your children's teachers and the school office. A teacher
appears once your child is in one of their classes.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · messages

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · classes
sources.content:
Classes, grades and teacher notes
Press 📚 Children's Classes, then open a class. You'll see three buttons:
| Button | What it shows
| 📝 Assignments | Everything set in the class and where your child stands on each.
| 📊 Children's Grades | A grade table. Change Quarter to All Time to see the whole year.
| 📝 Children's Notes | What the teacher has written about your child. Often the most useful screen.
If your child mentions work you can't see, the teacher may not have posted it yet.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · classes

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · extras
sources.content:
Calendar, activities, documents and re-enrolling
Calendar (on 🏠 Home): classes, due dates, tests and school events. Press
a day to see what's on it. With two or more children, pick whose calendar
with Select Child.
🏆 Activities: your children's sports and clubs, with the coach and
schedule.
📄 Documents: the handbook and school policies. Activities and Documents
are under 🧭 More at the bottom of 📊 Portal.
📋 Re-Enroll for Next Year (on 📊 Portal): opens the form with your
family's details already filled in. It's also how you update your address,
phone or emergency contacts.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · extras

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · settings
sources.content:
3 · Your settings
All on 👤 Profile in the top bar.
| To… | Use this card
| Choose which emails you get | 📧 Email Notifications: tick or untick, then Save Preferences.
| Change your password | 🔐 Change Password: type it twice, press Update Password.
| Change your sign-in email | ✉️ Change Email: type it twice, press Send Confirmation Link, then click the link sent to both the old and new address.
| Make the site easier to read | 🎨 Site Theme: choose Light. To make text bigger, press Ctrl and + (⌘ and + on a Mac).
| Sign out | ⚙️ Account Actions → 🚪 Logout. Always sign out on a shared computer.
You get two emails by default: when your child gets a new assignment, and
when their work is graded. Strike notices always come and can't be turned off.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · settings

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · help
sources.content:
4 · Help
Stuck? Find the message you see below. If it isn't here, email
learn@rivertech.me.
Also worth reading
Privacy Policy: what the school keeps and how to ask for it to be deleted.
Terms of Service: the agreement you accepted when you enrolled.
↑ Back to the top
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · help

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · stuck
sources.content:
If something goes wrong
| You see | Do this
| 👶 No Children Linked | Nothing is wrong. Link your child.
| This email is already registered | You already have an account. Sign in, or press Forgot Password?.
| Invalid login credentials | The email or password is wrong. Press Forgot Password?. The reset link works for one hour.
| ⚠️ This link is no longer valid | The email link was already used or has expired. Ask the office for a new one.
| This account has not been opened yet or ⚠️ Profile Incomplete | Email the office with the address you used.
| This account has been deactivated | Email the office. Nothing has been deleted.
| The school has sent too many sign-up emails… | Wait an hour and try again, or ask the office to set you up.
| 🔌 Couldn't load your account or 🔌 Can't reach the server | You're still signed in. Wait a minute and press Try again.
| A red bar: ⏰ This computer's clock is … ahead (or behind) | Your device's date or time is wrong. Turn on Set time automatically in your device's settings, then close and reopen the browser.
| No email arrives | Check spam. Check the address for typos. Then email the office from that address.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · stuck

sources.title: Parent Portal Guide · cannot
sources.content:
What only the office can change
Some details are kept by the school on purpose, because pickup lists and
emergencies depend on them. Email learn@rivertech.me
(or re-enroll) to change:
Your name, phone number or address
Emergency contacts, and who can pick up your child
Medical information
Your child's grade level or classes
Grades, attendance and strikes are changed by the teacher who gave them. The portal
doesn't handle fees or payments.
sources.keywords: Parent Portal Guide · cannot
